title: Allen, Tariq power Knight Riders to winning start
excerpt: Earlier in the day, Gulf Giants held their nerve to prevail over Sharjah Warriorz by 7 runs
author: Cricbuzz Staff
body: Gulf Giants made a thrilling start to their ILT20 campaign, securing a 7-run win over Sharjah Warriorz at the Sharjah Cricket Stadium on Sunday (November 7). Asked to bat first in an afternoon fixture, the Giants rode on Ibrahim Zadran’s sparkling 84 and David Miller’s 47 to post 168/8. A disciplined bowling effort, led by David Wiese (2/16) and Azmatullah Omarzai, then restricted the Warriorz to 161/7.

The Giants lost two wickets in the Powerplay, although Zadran was off the blocks quickly. Azmatullah Omarzai counter-attacked with a breezy 17 but after he and captain Heinrich Klaasen fell in quick succession, it was an 88-run stand between Zadran and Miller that revived the innings. Zadran struck six sixes in his 53-ball knock before falling to Junaid Siddique, who was the pick of the Warriorz bowlers. The innings then ended with two wickets off the last two balls, including a run out, as only 21 runs came off the last three overs.

Tim Seifert and Paul Walter then blazed away for the Warriorz, with 24 runs coming off the fourth over bowled by Alzarri Joseph. Walter’s 24-ball 40 set the foundation up for the chase, but regular wickets stunted their progress despite James Vince anchoring them with a 26-ball 31. They eventually needed 41 off the last four overs and a masterful death bowling display by Omarzai and Wiese left the Warriorz requiring 20 off the last. Joseph speared a wide down the leg-side to the fence and conceded a boundary, but he held his nerve as Mohammad Nabi fell off the last ball for 39.

Brief Scores: Gulf Giants 168/8 in 20 overs (Ibrahim Zadran 84, David Miller 47; Junaid Siddique 2-30, Adam Milne 2-33) beat Sharjah Warriorz 161/7 in 20 overs (Paul Walter 40, Mohammad Nabi 39; David Wiese 2-16, Haider Razzaq 1-24) by 7 runs.
Abu Dhabi Knight Riders vs Dubai Capitals

Abu Dhabi Knight Riders kickstarted their campaign with a resounding 55-run victory over Dubai Capitals at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium. Finn Allen's 74 and Andre Fletcher's 55 set the tone as the duo forged 119-run opening stand as the Knight Riders scored 167/6, before Usman Tariq's 4 for 27 and Muhammad Rohid Khan's 3 for 11 bowled the Capitals out for 112 in 17.5 overs.

The Knight Riders picked up pace after mustering just 13 off the first 3.5 overs as Allen broke free with a six. There was no stopping his mojo as he accelerated to a 29-ball fifty, taking Marcus Stoinis down in a 23-run 11th over. He was soon bowled by Noor Ahmad, forcing a slowdown as the Capitals’ bowlers bounced back despite Fletcher getting to his fifty. The West Indian opener took 49 balls for his 55 and was also bowled by Noor and a spurt of late wickets meant that the Knight Riders never got the final kick they were after.

As it turned out though, their total of 167 proved more than sufficient. Rohid struck twice in the second over to remove Faf du Plessis and Masood Gurbaz, before Jason Holder dismissed Max Holden soon after. At 6 for 3, the Capitals were in dire straits and it got worse when Sam Billings and Hassan Khan fell in successive overs. Usman Tariq then ran through the lower order and despite Stoinis’ 32-ball 47, the result was a formality as Rohid castled Noor to wrap things up.

Brief Scores: Abu Dhabi Knight Riders 167/6 in 20 overs (Finn Allen 74, Andre Fletcher 55; Karim Janat 2-8, Dushmantha Chameera 2-25) beat Dubai Capitals 112 in 17.5 overs (Marcus Stoinis 47; Usman Tariq 4-27, Muhammad Rohid Khan 3-11, Sunil Narine 1-12) by 55 runs.
